title: Compound and complex sentences: joining ideas

blocks.content: Short sentences are clear, but joining them makes your writing flow. Let's learn two ways to join ideas into one sentence.
A compound sentence joins two complete sentences with and, but or or.

steps: Two complete sentences: 'I was tired.' and 'I kept going.'
Join them with 'but': 'I was tired, but I kept going.'

blocks.prompt: Join with 'and': She sang. He danced.
blocks.explain: Join the two complete ideas with 'and': She sang and he danced.
blocks.rule: A compound sentence joins two complete sentences with and, but or or.

practiceItems.prompt: join with 'and': I read. I slept.
join with 'but': It was small. It was strong.
practiceItems.answer: It was small but it was strong

practiceItems.prompt: join with 'or': We can walk. We can run.
practiceItems.answer: We can walk or we can run

practiceItems.prompt: join with 'and': He cooked. She cleaned.

blocks.content: A complex sentence adds a part that starts with because, when, if or although. That part cannot stand alone.

blocks.prompt: Add the joining word (a reason): I stayed inside ___ it was raining.
blocks.explain: 'because' gives the reason, making a complex sentence: I stayed inside because it was raining.
blocks.rule: A complex sentence adds a part beginning with because, when, if or although.

practiceItems.prompt: reason word: I was happy ___ we won
time word: ___ the bell rang, we left
condition word: ___ it rains, we stay in
reason word: she smiled ___ she passed

blocks.content: Compound joins two whole ideas with and/but/or; complex adds a because/when/if part. Both make your writing flow. Let's practise!
